transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having these times where, after a really long day on site or a neighborhood meeting, I get home and just eat way more than I meant to. Like leftover takeout, cereal, chips… whatever’s around. And then I’m uncomfortably full.
After you've eaten a lot like that, do you ever try to make up for it by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Yeah… sometimes. Not laxatives or anything, but a few times a month I’ll, um… go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. I just get panicky that I’ve messed everything up, like all the effort I put into looking put-together.
How often do you find yourself making yourself throw up after eating, and does it usually happen in response to specific situations or emotions?

Um… not every time. Maybe a few times a month, usually after those nights where I feel like I’ve eaten too much. I just start panicking that I’ve undone everything, like… all the effort to look okay and put-together, and then I’ll go make myself throw up.
When you make yourself throw up, is it mainly because you feel you’ve eaten too much, or is it more about how you feel about your body or weight?

It’s… both, I guess. It starts with feeling like I ate too much, but then it turns into how I look. Since I’ve been wearing more fitted work clothes and being up front in meetings, I kind of judge the whole day by whether my pants feel tight or if I think people can see my stomach.
When you’re feeling upset about eating too much and decide to make yourself throw up, do you feel that it’s mainly about keeping your weight down, or more about how you see your body shape overall?

I guess it’s more about how I think I look… my shape, I mean. Like since I’ve been wearing more fitted work clothes and I’m in front of people more, I’ll get stuck on whether my pants feel tight or if my stomach shows. It kind of ruins the whole day in my head.
When you make yourself throw up, is it more about trying to keep your weight from going up, or is it more about how you see your body shape — like seeing yourself as larger than you actually are?

More the shape thing, I think. Like… since I’ve had to wear more fitted work clothes and be up front in meetings, I get really stuck on whether my pants feel tight or if people can see my stomach. It kind of decides how I feel about the whole day.
